sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface expression confirmed by flow cytometry with anti-His-tag antibody; endogenous EVI2B function not independently assayed in the tagged construct.
sites.rationale: The paper places the His-tag 'N-terminal to the full-length EVI2B sequence' (L1). EVI2B carries a signal peptide at residues 1–21; any tag upstream of the cleavage site would be co-translationally removed and could not be detected on the cell surface. Because L2 demonstrates surface detection by anti-His-tag antibody, the tag must reside after the SP cleavage site, i.e., at the mature N-terminus (insert_after_residue = 21, between S21 and K22). EVI2B has exactly one extracellular terminus (residues 22–204 precede the single TM helix at 205–225), so the position is unambiguously topology_derived. Python confirmed residue 21 = S and residue 22 = K from the canonical sequence. His-tagged full-length EVI2B expressed transiently (pcDNA3.1/EVI2B) and stably (pAS3w.Ppuro/EVI2B) in human cells; L1 states the His-tag was inserted N-terminal to the full-length EVI2B coding sequence; L2 confirms surface display of the His-tag by flow cytometry with anti-His-tag antibody.

sources.claim: After 48 h, surface expression of EVI2B or CXCR2 was determined by Western blotting and by flow cytometry with mouse anti-EVI2B Ab (Thermo Fisher Scientific, MEM-216), anti-CXCR2 Ab (R&D Systems, MAB331), or anti-His tag Ab as described above.

literature_notes: All three ledger lines (L1, L2, L3) describe the same His-tagged EVI2B construct and the same N-terminal junction; they do not pin separate residues or separate loops, so only one site is reported. No residue number is stated in any line, but the combination of 'N-terminal to the full-length sequence' (L1) and confirmed surface detection of the His-tag (L2) uniquely resolves the junction to after the signal-peptide cleavage site (residue 21/22). No internal extracellular loop insertions, C-terminal tags, or intracellular insertions are reported in the ledger.
